extracted.intended_audience: newspaper readers and wire/newshouse editors (people who compile or read AP-style news dispatches)
extracted.subtask_description: Assembling and writing short, datelined wire dispatches for a news homepage or print front page: concise leads, clear datelines, attributions, numbers, quotes and brief contextual background across multiple international items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include clear dateline and source tag
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin items with a dateline showing location and date and tag the source (e.g., 'PARIS, MARCH 26=(AP)=', 'TUNIS, MARCH 26=CAP)-').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the city, date and the wire/service abbreviation exactly as in examples on the page so readers immediately know where and when the dispatch originated. Multiple items on one page should each have their own dateline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise lead summarizing the main fact
rubrics_metrics.description: Start each dispatch with a short, punchy lead that states the central news (e.g., 'FRANCE CRACKED DOWN WITH A HEAVY FIST ON TUNISIA'S INDEPENDENCE-SEEKING NATIONALISTS TODAY, ARRESTING PREMIER...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lead should answer the who/what/where/when in one or two sentences to allow fast scanning on a homepage or front page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute to authoritative sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute claims and reports to named sources such as government officials, agencies, or the wire service (e.g., 'the French press agency reported', 'the command said', 'State Department witnesses testified').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear whether an assertion is an official claim, an agency dispatch, or reporter observation to preserve accuracy and avoid presenting unverified claims as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use direct quotations for key on-record statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Include verbatim quotes when relaying important positions or statements (examples: 'I HAVE DECIDED TO PREVENT...,' 'IS AN AMERICAN GANGSTER AND SHOULD HAVE BEEN HANGED').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, attributable quotes add authority and color; ensure punctuation and attribution are precise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report precise numbers and counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific numerical details for casualties, arrests, production figures and other measurable facts (e.g., '160 persons have been injured and 74 jailed', 'Western Europe's total steel output rose from 92,516,000 to 98,092,000 metric tons').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where numbers are given, include units, timeframes and comparisons where useful; if figures are estimates or disputed, indicate that in the copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include brief background and context
rubrics_metrics.description: Give concise historical or political background connecting the current event to prior developments (e.g., references to the 1948 declaration on Trieste, past riots, prior martial law proclamations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One or two sentences of context help readers understand significance without diverting from the immediate news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain neutral, factual tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Use objective descriptive language focused on facts, even when reporting charged events (the page's dispatches report violence, accusations and propaganda while largely avoiding editorializing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid loaded adjectives unless in quoted material; balance accounts by attributing contentious claims to sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire-style brevity and short paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Write in short, clipped paragraphs and sentences suitable for rapid scanning and editing by downstream desks (observed throughout the dispatches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep paragraphs to one or two sentences; prefer active verbs and straightforward constructions to speed comprehension and layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group related short items on a single page
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect multiple short dispatches—each with its dateline/lead—on one page or column so readers get a rapid round-up of international developments (the page contains many such short items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear separators or headlines (e.g., 'NIGHT LEAD URANIUM') and consistent formatting so editors and readers can pick items for prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness cues and present-tense markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Signal currency with words like 'today', 'tonight', and explicit dates to emphasize immediacy (frequent use of 'today', 'tonight', and explicit March 26 datelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timestamps/dates are accurate and match the dateline; timeliness is critical for homepage/front-page placement decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance immediate facts with official reactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Include official reactions, government positions, and international responses alongside event reporting (examples: Achenson's news conference remarks, French government broadcasts, UN mentions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present both event description and official/strategic implications succinctly so readers and editors see both the incident and its diplomatic/political fallout.
